text:
Alex Chen: got SLO alert - hosted-infer us-west2 p99 spike and a few customer timeouts reported, kicking this off 09:08am
Kim Rivera: saw that, p99 jumped from ~140ms to ~1.2s at 09:06-09:09, p95 also impacted
SRE Bot: alert: SLO burn rule "hosted-infer.gateway.latency.p99" fired (region=us-west2) — 09:09
Maria Gonzales: support reports: two customers opened tickets with 502/504 and timeouts, tickets CUST-5012 and CUST-5017, one included trace id a7c9d2e
Dev Support: customer repro curl:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
# -> HTTP/2 504 or stalled
```
Alex Chen: quick checks: 5xx fraction across gateway spiked to ~7% at 09:06, auth failures (401/403) slightly up too — pulling logs
Kim Rivera: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted-infer/latency?var-region=us-west2 — panels show spike aligns with an authz latency bump
Tim O'Neill: tracing: a7c9d2e sample shows long proxy handshake (2.8s) then upstream connection reset; model-host spans missing for some traces
Maria Gonzales: added runbook step: verify batcher queues and prefetch queue around spike window
Alex Chen: batcher_v2 backlog metric shows 2.8x normal around 09:05-09:10, concurrent batches queued, possible head-of-line blocking
SRE Bot: deploy bot: no deploys in us-west2 during window (last deploy 07:55)
Tim O'Neill: ran a filter for handshake errors:
```
service=hosted-infer component=proxy handshake_reset=true | stats count by upstream_host
```
Tim O'Neill: shows elevated resets on model-b-07 and model-b-08 at 09:06-09:07
Alex Chen: i'm going to drain model-b-07/08 and apply fallback policy to route new requests to smaller variants in us-west2 for now
Dev Support: replied to customers CUST-5012/5017: "We see intermittent timeouts and have rerouted traffic; investigating, will update in 30m" :thumbsup:
Kim Rivera: after draining and fallback (10:02) p99 fell back near baseline by 10:08, 5xx fraction down to 0.9%
Maria Gonzales: exported traces and pinned dashboard for postmortem; collecting KMS and authz metrics for correlation
Alex Chen: hypothesis: model-hosts had transient network/handshake instability and auth token refresh/latency amplified head-of-line effects in proxy -> caused gateway 5xx cascade
Tim O'Neill: next steps: 1) run targeted handshake stress against model-b-08 in staging to repro, 2) validate token cache behavior and KMS latencies for that timeframe, 3) tune alert to fire on combined auth+gateway 5xx signal not just latency
Maria Gonzales: opening postmortem ticket and attaching traces + logs + customer timelines
Alex Chen: thanks all — will keep this thread updated if we see other affected customers or repeat patterns
SRE Bot: action: reroute policy applied to us-west2 at 10:02 by Alex Chen
